questions.q: In 'The Miller, His Son, and the Ass', where were the Miller and his Son taking the Ass?
choices: To the river for a drink
questions.evidence: on their way to market with an Ass which they hoped to sell

questions.q: In 'The Miller, His Son, and the Ass', what did the Miller do after the merchants told the boy to respect old age?
choices: Made the boy get down and rode himself
questions.evidence: he made the boy get down and climbed up himself to ride

questions.q: In 'The Miller, His Son, and the Ass', why did the Miller keep changing who rode the Ass?
choices: He was trying to please the people on the road

questions.q: In 'The Miller, His Son, and the Ass', what happened to the Ass at the end?
choices: He fell off the bridge into the river
He was sold for a high price
He ran away to the hills
He was given to the merchants
questions.evidence: down he tumbled into the river

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Miller, His Son, and the Ass'?
choices: If you try to please all, you please none
questions.evidence: If you try to please all, you please none.

questions.q: In 'The Ant and the Dove', how did the Dove save the Ant?
choices: She dropped a blade of straw beside it
She picked it up in her beak
She pushed it with her wing
questions.evidence: the Dove dropped a blade of straw close beside it

questions.q: In 'The Ant and the Dove', the Ant stung the man so the Dove could escape. What is the lesson?
In 'The Man and the Satyr', why did the Satyr leave?

questions.evidence: A fellow that blows hot and cold in the same breath cannot be friends with me!
